title: Advanced Aggregations: DISTINCT & CASE 🧠
description: Count unique values, and use conditional logic inside aggregate functions.

slides.title: Counting Unique Values 🔢
slides.content:
# DISTINCT Inside COUNT

`COUNT(DISTINCT column)` counts the number of distinct (unique) values in a column.

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer) AS unique_customers FROM orders;
```

This tells you how many different customers placed orders, not how many orders.

quizData.question: If the orders table has customers [A, B, A, C, B], what does `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer)` return?

slides.title: Multiple Distinct Aggregates 📊
slides.content:
You can count distinct in different columns:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer) AS cust_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT region) AS region_count
FROM orders;
```

But you cannot do `COUNT(DISTINCT *)` – you must specify a column.

slides.title: Conditional Aggregation with CASE 🎯
slides.content:
# The Power of CASE Inside Aggregates

`CASE` expression creates conditional values inside an aggregate.

```sql
SELECT
    SUM(CASE WHEN region = 'East' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS east_total,
    SUM(CASE WHEN region = 'West' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS west_total
FROM orders;
```

This pivots data horizontally – great for reports.

slides.title: Conditional SUM Example
slides.content: Compute per‑region totals in separate columns:
slides.codeSnippet:
SELECT
    SUM(CASE WHEN region = 'East' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS East,
    SUM(CASE WHEN region = 'West' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS West,
    SUM(CASE WHEN region = 'North' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS North
FROM orders;

quizData.question: What does `COUNT(CASE WHEN amount > 200 THEN 1 END)` count?
quizData.explanation: For rows where condition is true, CASE returns 1 (counted); otherwise NULL (ignored by COUNT).

slides.title: Conditional COUNT for Frequency 🔢
slides.content:
Count how many orders are 'large' (>300) and 'small' (≤300) per customer:

```sql
SELECT customer,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN amount > 300 THEN 1 END) AS large_orders,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN amount <= 300 THEN 1 END) AS small_orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer;
```

slides.title: CASE COUNT Example
slides.codeSnippet:
SELECT customer,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN amount > 300 THEN 1 END) AS high,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN amount <= 300 THEN 1 END) AS low
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer;

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Pivot Tables with Conditional Aggregates

This technique is how you manually create pivot tables in SQL when your database doesn’t have a PIVOT function.

slides.title: Advanced Aggregation Practice 🏋️
slides.content:
Using the `orders` table:
1. Count how many distinct customers placed orders.
2. Write a query that shows total revenue for each region in separate columns (East, West, North) in a single row.
3. Show for each customer the number of orders above 200 and below or equal to 200.

slides.title: Advanced Aggregations Done 🎉
slides.content: Now you can count unique values and conditionally aggregate. Next, we'll put everything together in real reports.
